FN-E55P99-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 322
Committee: Judiciary Sponsor: Senator Sam Givhan
Analyst: Riley Aaron Date: 05/23/2023
Senate Bill 322 as introduced would increase receipts collected by judges of probate for the
issuance of notary commissions by an estimated $6.5 million for each four year period
beginning in January 2026, based on the $90 fee increase to be collected from an estimated
73,000 active notaries statewide. The receipts would be distributed among the various counties
or judges of probate of those counties. In addition, this bill increases the required bond amount
to be held by notaries public from $25,000 to $50,000, which would increase the obligations of
state and local agencies that pay the cost of bonds for persons employed by such agencies. This
bill would also increase the fee notaries public are entitled to receive for each notary transaction
from $5 under current law to $10.
Finally, this bill could increase receipts to the State General Fund and municipal general funds
from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, municipal general
funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of
the State General Fund, local jails, the district attorneys, the Department of Corrections, the
Bureau of Pardons and Paroles, and community corrections programs by an undetermined
amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses
provided by this bill and the penalties imposed.

FN-E55P99-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 322
Committee: Judiciary Sponsor: Senator Sam Givhan
Analyst: Riley Aaron Date: 05/30/2023
Senate Bill 322 as passed the Senate would increase receipts of judges of probate for the
issuance of notary commissions by an estimated $1.6 million annually based on the $90 fee
increase (collected every four years) from an estimated 71,367 active notaries statewide. The
receipts would be distributed among the various counties or judges of probate of those counties.
In addition, this bill would increase the required bond amount to be held by notaries public from
$25,000 to $50,000, which would increase the obligations of state and local agencies that pay
the cost of bonds for persons employed by such agencies. This bill would also increase the fee
notaries public are entitled to receive for each notary transaction from $5, under current law, to
$10.
Finally, this bill could increase receipts to the State General Fund and municipal general funds
from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, municipal general
funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of
the State General Fund, local jails, the district attorneys, the Department of Corrections, the
Bureau of Pardons and Paroles, and community corrections programs by an undetermined
amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses
provided by this bill and the penalties imposed.
